This game got my attention back then when it was announced.
But due to review from launch, i refrain my self from buying the game at the time and decide to just wait for the right time.
Sadly, the player number has been going down since then...

But. after watching a youtuber name "Bigfry TV" and hear what he has to say about the game, i decide to give it a try and support the dev. And i was actually surprised. I could say this is probably one of my favourite arcade-ish modern combat fps out there.

For the record, i played games like BF4, BF1, R6 Siege, Insurgency: Sandstorm, etc and i compare this with those kind of game and for an indie game, the game is good.

:: Pros ::

- Customization: Deep customization on character as well as your weapon load out. There's a lot of customization option ranging from choice of weapons, attachments, parts, camo, clothing, type of armor and helmets, ability/type of UAV. And for balance, the heavier your load out, the slower you are so don't worry about a guy with rpg running around at the speed of sound. All can be earn using in game currency and it's fairly easy to get money just buy playing. What i mean by playing is to actually level up. it's not that hard to get level really. Oh fair warning, as of now progress in different server IS separated.

- Gameplay: Good and fun gameplay. I like it. It takes a fair ammount of time to kill people, it's pretty satisfying to kill the enemy, reload time isn't as ridiculous as in games like COD, recoil is fair, gun felt nice, and surprisingly, making tanks etc as spawnable "ability" (or whatever its called) does bring some sort of balance to the game. Also, at the start of a match, you are asked whether you can to be offensive or defensive. depend on what you choose, you'll be rewarded more point for either attack or defend a point.

- Maps and Modes: There are 2 mode (TDM and Warzone-capture the point type with 2 point control system) There are quite a few maps you can play in + modified ver of said map for certain mode.

Good Visual: It looks nice. cool to see u shot body armor or metal helmet etc and there's effect for it. But, it does come with a cost. For optimization, i'll talk about it more in a few points down below.

- High Ping compensation: due to low population, i need to play in EU (i'm from SEA) and surprisingly it went well. For you who don't know, there's 2 type of high ping. Due to lag or due to distance and in my case it's because of distance. The game is playable still even tho i had 150-200 ish ping. And no, i'm not invinsible or hard to kill because of it. i'm very much as easy to kill as you normally would.

:: Cons ::

- Animation: Felt clunky at times, specially during running, crouch, prone movement change, as well as going thru obstacle. But it's nothing too major and considering it's an indie dev it's more understandable.

- Optimization: this game still need to be more optimized. From what i've seen, it's either a hit or miss. Some people could run the game just fine, some struggle to get decent fps especially in warzone, and some are something in between. UE4 stuff. we can only hope that it would get better overtime. with this in mind, if you are new and want to buy the game, buy it and IMMEDIATELY benchmark the settings etc, see if you can run it. Try to play warzone instead of TDM for benchmark, use server browser instead of quick match find.

- Population: Yes, this game has a rather low player base number. what it direly need now is more playerbase. DON'T be discouraged from buying because of low playerbase. the game isn't dead, it still got player base that play from time to time. it isn't that big, but it's still there. And i'll give the dev benefit of the doubt and believe that they are indeed still working on more modes and content, as well as optimization before full release.

This game have mixed review yes, but the old review are from during the rough launch and the new one are from technical issue as well as low pop. But it isn't as bad as some people might make it seems like.  Hope to see you in game!

World War 3 has the foundation to become amazing. Even now, it is a superb game that borrows the best features from a variety of games and blends them into something new. 

The gunplay feels like Insurgency, the gameplay feels like Battlefield, and the advanced features and squad mechanics feel like Squad. You can play as a lone wolf, sure, but there is definitely a lot of room for squad gameplay and coordination. Vehicle combat reminds me of Bad Company. It is by far my favorite aspect of the game. 

As the new maps, features, and content roll out, World War 3 could very well end up being a true sucessor to Battlefield, and perhaps be even better.

This isn't the most in-depth review, but it's a casual one with some pros and cons. Probably only a 5-minute read, but I think includes all you need to know at the moment. 

I know most people are looking at WW3, in search of a Battlefield replacement, and after 20+ hours now of playing the game, I can safely say it does that job, for me. There are certainly some negatives, but I think the positives definitely outweigh them. After disappointing news the open beta has been delayed, I bit the bullet and dropped £10 or so on the game, and have certainly not regretted doing so. From my experience over the last 20 hours, these are the pros and cons in my eyes.

Pros:

- The gunplay is incredible. Running around as an infantry player feels awesome. Peaking corners, holding angles, waiting for enemies at choke points, it feels great. There doesn't feel like there's much if any bloom, which is really nice. There's a massive Tarkov-esque selection of weapons and attachments, all of which can be set up to suit your individual playstyle. Obviously, attachments and better weapons are obtained by leveling up, character, and then the individual weapons, but nothing feels unobtainable, and so far what I've unlocked has felt worth the commitment. The current level cap at the time of writing this review is 51. Don't feel like you're going to be behind if you want to wait until the open beta either, as the game will wipe all progress once that happens, and everyone will be back on a level playing field. 

----- A gunplay/customization sidenote. Every attachment feels like it does what it says on the tin. If you wanted to play from range, unlock the barrel for a gun that increases damage at range, use a 3/4x optic, and run the higher damage ammo type. If you want to play up close, use the opposite. Sniping is a great option, so is running from point to point with a sub. AR's can be used both at close-range and long-range. Shotguns are also a viable option. The possibilities are really endless, and it's kept me so far, after 20 hours, feeling like I haven't even scratched the surface. 

- The maps, albeit only 4 of them for Tactical Ops, play really well, on foot. It's basically Conquest Small, but all of them can be navigated on foot without feeling like you're miles away from a fight. There's also plenty of cover, unlike 2042. If you're looking for some casual Team Deathmatch action, that works really well also. Best out of 3 rounds wins the match. The maps are designed well, there are plenty of routes between objectives, lots of flanking opportunities, and definitely enough windows/vantage points for those who like to play the objective from a distance. 

- Killstreaks/point streaks, whatever you wanna call them. They're cool. There's a range of UAV options, a range of airstrike options, and a range of vehicles you're able to call in, either to control or assist you in various ways. If you play the Tac' Ops mode with a good squad, you can rack up so many points just running UAV's and using your airstrikes well. It's great fun. Each one has different point requirements, you can either stack your points for a high-end airstrike or use them as soon as you obtain them, and call in UAV's to help your squad. 

- The backpack. I've seen some people complaining about this, saying it's useless, but I think the opposite. Your backpack is a backpack you have in-game, that you can fill with different attachments and tacticals. Some of which aren't available via the standard customization screen. If you have a 3x optic attached to your weapon and feel like you're engaged in more close-quarters combat, press 'i' and change your optic. Standard customization isn't available on the fly, and I like that. Some people will not. It's very much a marmite feature. 

The negatives are, and I'll only speak from personal experience here, but I know a lot of people have complained about server availability, connection issues, and the separate game launcher. 

- The tanks. Make an anti-tank class as early as you can. Run mines, a rocket launcher, and an ammo box. And then pray that they don't spot you trying to take them out, because they'll just blast you into thin air. A couple of the objectives on a couple of the maps are borderline unobtainable if there's a tank sitting on them. Plus, they can drive back to their spawn when they're low on health and heal up, so if you think you're doing well getting it down to 10-20% health, think again.

- Servers. Now, I'm playing from the U.K, and I've had no connectivity issues whatsoever, and it seems harsh for me to even mention it, being as the game is still in closed beta, but it doesn't appear there are any dedicated regional servers. The game just finds 40 players from anywhere in the world and slings them into a lobby. If you're playing from outside of Europe, you might find it a little ropey. I've had a few guys from South America and Asia in my games, complaining of the experience. 

- The launcher. It's weird. If you buy the game from Steam, go to the WW3 website, and download the launcher separately. Link your Steam account on the website, and download the game that way. Don't do it through Steam. Or, if you do, make sure you click stop, as it'll count as play time whilst the game is downloading and therefore will mean you're not able to get a refund if you don't like it. 

- There are only 4 maps for Tac' Ops. It's a beta, and I don't think this really is a negative, but if you're going to be putting in some serious hours, they might get a bit boring. Hopefully, they'll add another when it goes open beta. 

There are a few other small positives and a few other small negatives, but I don't think they need mentioning. Remember the game is still in beta, and you'll be fine.

I don't love making this review, because there was a window there in 2022 and 2023 where I absolutely loved this game. WW3 was one of those projects with a good core gameplay loop but was always let down by something else: too little content, too few updates, poor server performance, a crappy launcher, too much focus on microtransactions when still trying to establish a player base, and other overall mismanagement issues.

In 2025, what we have is a game without a player base. New ownership has picked up the game and is delivering updates, but at this point it is a drip-feed of tweaks and additions being handed to a player base that doesn't exist. The game has averaged fewer than 200 players since January 2024, and that has now dropped to fewer than 100 players. Trying to play this game is often an exercise of ending up in a waiting room with 3 other players, and watching people join and quit one-by-one.

The positives for the game are still there. The gameplay is a more hardcore Battlefield style experience. Weapon recoil is stronger than Battlefield's often laser-y guns. Movement is weightier and should appeal to players who think BF is drifting too close to COD-style movement. Weapon customization is also a major strong point of the game, and an area where the project punches way above its weight.

Bought this game not expecting to like it, but turns out I was pleasantly suprised. The game is very much like battlefield. Better in a lot of ways but worse in others. Although it has tanks and vehicles in it, it's much more of an infantry game than battlefield which suits me as I don't get into the vehicle combat all that much. The map designs so far are very good. I like realistic shooters, but not so realistic that they take the fun out of the game. I find this game to be a good balance between realistic and fun. It's a little more realistic than battlefield but not so much that it is boring like squad "sorry if you like squad.. i'm not a fan". One thing I really like is the damage system. This game has best damage system I have seen in a shooter since counterstrike. It actually registers the shots where they hit you. So if you hit someone in the hand for instance... it's gonna register a hand shot and do an appropriate amount of damage.. Very similar to counterstrikes damage system but with several different levels of armor. You can hit a guy in his armor plate and only do 10 damage but hit him a few inches below the armor plate in the stomach and do 80 damage. I can't stress enough how well they did  the damage system as it's one thing that so many shooters get wrong. Not in this game though. I am also really happy that I am able to turn hitmarkers off in this game. I can't stand hit markers or similar kiddie stuff, so it's really nice I can turn them off. Actually my biggest gripe with the game is that wish I could turn off bullet tracers also so I wouldn't see my bullets flying through the air, and they need more game modes & maps... but besides that the game is fantastic. In my opinion farm51 has greatly improved on the battlefield formula and made a very enjoyable game. Looking forward to it getting better as more maps and content is released. 5 out of 5.
